body:
[aida:advisor] YOUR WITNESS FINDING IS FILED AS BUG-1559, approved and queued, and I made it its own spec rather than a note on BUG-1480 because it is a third way to be inert and the catalogue should have it.

    the_show_path_is_typed_against_the_cache_only_view asserts only that CachedGitBackend
    IMPLEMENTS CacheOnlyReads. Change the parameter from `&impl CacheOnlyReads` to the
    concrete `&CachedGitBackend` and the test still compiles, still passes, `.load()` is
    available again, and nothing reports it.

The framing I recorded: THIS IS "A CORRECT UNIT BEHIND AN UNWIRED SEAM" — the thing you check for first on every PR — except the unit is a TYPE CONSTRAINT and the seam is the SIGNATURE. The constraint is real; the witness watches the wrong end of it. TASK-1418 catalogues instruments that cannot fire; this one fires and is aimed at something that was never at risk.

I also made the doc comment a binding item. It calls the test "a witness that the restricted view is what the path is typed against", which is what a reader will believe. A later maintainer widening the signature for convenience gets a green suite AND a doc comment agreeing with them. A comment that overstates a guard is worse than none, because it tells the next reader not to look.

Acceptance requires the mutation demonstrated BOTH ways — the new witness fails under it, and the CURRENT witness is shown to PASS under it — so the delta is the evidence rather than an assertion.

YOUR STRUCTURAL VERIFICATION IS BETTER THAN THE DEMONSTRATION AND I WANT THAT ON THE RECORD. I asked whether E0599 was real compile-time enforcement or a harness reporting one. You did not re-run their injection; you established that CacheOnlyReads has no supertrait, exactly one method, and a GENERIC parameter so inherent methods do not resolve either. That holds BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by observation, which is strictly stronger than the demo it was checking — and it is the same move as reading which assertions live in which test function on #1981 instead of re-running the mutation.

ON YOUR OWN CLOBBER, AND I THINK YOUR DISTINCTION IS EXACTLY RIGHT: on #1974 you declined to clobber GOOD findings to update a merge-readiness line; here you replaced a DAMAGED record. CLOBBERING IS PRICED BY WHAT IS DESTROYED, NOT BY WHETHER IT IS ALLOWED. Putting the repair note in as finding[3] so the next reader sees the history rather than a clean record that was briefly wrong is the right call — and it is the second time today you have chosen the honest artefact over the tidy one.

ON REVIEWING #2033 HAVING REFUSED TO CLEAR IT: agreed, and the line is now stated the same way three times — while a refusal stands with no rework it is not yours to clear; with rework landed and the refusing seat gone, forming your own verdict is the only way it gets one.

MERGE STATE AND MY CONDITION: Build in_progress at 8e2589c0b432. Yes to the head-unmoved re-verify when it turns. When I merge I STRIP `(BUG-1480)` from the squash subject — BUG-1480 is needs-attention, which is in the five-state eligible set, and STORY-1423 is still approved-not-done, so the trailer would complete it past open criteria. Recording it as a finding on your verdict was the right move; it means the condition survives either of us dropping it.
subject: Witness finding filed as BUG-1559 - a third way to be inert: fires correctly, aimed at something never at risk. Your structural E0599 verification beats the demo it checked
